title: Which statements does the rocket graph justify?
description: Six statements about the rocket launch graph are tested one by one against the bars, and the world total for the latest year is estimated. Keeko thinks all organisations launched more every year because the SpaceX bars keep growing.
teaching_notes: One idea: a statement is justified only when the bars it names prove it, by reading, adding or averaging. Watch for students who accept a statement about all organisations after looking at one tall group.

source: Rocket launch graph: which of statements (a) to (f) can be justified, and estimate the total number of rockets launched worldwide in the latest year
video_script.why: The child can read the rocket graph and now tests statements against it by totals and averages.
video_script.substitution: The book's own six statements and its four options for the world total.
video_script.anchor: Rocket launches in three years: CASC 48, 35, 45; Roscosmos 16, 21, 18; Arianespace 15, 6, 3; ISRO 2, 5, 7; Galactic Energy 1, 2, 7; SpaceX 31, 61, 96. Latest-year bars of the rest: Rocket Lab 9, United Launch Alliance 3, Expace 6, Others 26.
video_script.wrong_answer: all organisations launched more every year
video_script.wrong_move: Accepts a statement about all organisations after looking at the fast growing SpaceX bars, without checking the groups that fell.
video_script.payoff_line: Statements b, c, d and e are justified, and the world total is about two hundred and twenty.

final_answer.value: Justified: (b), (c), (d) and (e); not justified: (a) and (f); 2023 total about 220, option (b)
final_answer.spoken: statements b, c, d and e are justified; the total is about two hundred and twenty

maths_rules: (a) Arianespace 15, 6, 3 and CASC 48, 35 fall, so not justified
(b) only SpaceX, from the USA, passes 50 (61 and 96); CASC's highest is about 48, so justified
(e) ISRO 2 + 5 + 7 = 14 and Galactic Energy 1 + 2 + 7 = 10; 14 > 10, so justified
(f) Roscosmos 16 + 21 + 18 = 55, less than 60, so not justified
latest-year total: 96 + 45 + 18 + 3 + 9 + 3 + 7 + 7 + 6 + 26 = 220, which is in 200 to 400
video_script.design: One idea: find the bars a statement names, then add or average them and compare. The readings sit in the anchor; each statement is tested on the board and gets a tick or a cross.
open_questions: The bar readings for CASC, Roscosmos, Rocket Lab, United Launch Alliance, Expace and Others come from the worklist; the extracted book text does not give them. The book says Others is around 25 in the latest year while the worklist uses 26; both give a total of about 220. Check against the printed graph.
